title: Florida House, District 23
what_it_does: Represents District 23 in the Florida House of Representatives; votes on state laws and the state budget.
decided_note: Republican Rep. J.J. Grow won the Aug. 18, 2026 closed Republican primary with about 73% over Tod Cloud. A closed party primary was held Aug. 18, 2026, which under Florida law means at least one other candidate (opposing-party, no-party or write-in) qualified for the Nov. 3 general election; that opponent's name could not be verified from search snippets.
verified_ballot_note: Florida Politics (Aug. 18, 2026) reported Grow won the HD 23 Republican primary with 73% (https://floridapolitics.com/archives/814627-jj-grow-bests-tod-cloud-in-hd-23-republican-primary/); ClickOrlando's voter guide labels the race a 'Republican primary' (not a universal primary), which implies a November opponent. Ballotpedia's Grow page also references a Nov. 3, 2026 general election (https://ballotpedia.org/J.J._Grow). The November opponent's name was not found. Research limitation: every WebFetch (Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, Division of Elections, county SOEs, news sites) was blocked and the search budget was capped, so this roster comes only from search-result snippets and should be re-verified against the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: J.J. Grow
candidates.occupation: Businessman and entrepreneur; state representative for District 23
candidates.background: Incumbent Republican state representative for HD 23 (Citrus County and the Dunnellon area of Marion County). Won the Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary over Tod Cloud with about 73%.
candidates.primary_result: Won Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary with ~73% over Tod Cloud (Florida Politics)

taxes.summary: Grow's campaign site says he voted to cut billions of dollars in taxes, including sales-tax holidays for school supplies, tools and hurricane-preparedness items, and for balanced budgets that reduced spending and paid off a billion dollars in state debt early.

property_tax.summary: Grow says he voted to place a property-tax relief measure on the 2026 ballot that he says could save homeowners thousands of dollars a year, and describes lowering property taxes as a way to keep Floridians in their homes. A local voter guide noted he did not answer how he personally would vote on the amendment.

sources.title: 2026 Voter's Guide - Florida House District 23, Republican primary

insurance.summary: Grow credits market-based changes, including limits on what he calls frivolous lawsuits, for bringing new insurers into Florida and lowering rates, and says the job now is to stay vigilant that carriers pay claims and do not hide profits. He does not propose rate caps or expanding Citizens.

housing.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

immigration.summary: Grow says he voted to secure Florida's borders and to work with federal partners against illegal immigration, and for what he calls record funding for detention and deportation of criminal illegal aliens. He also backs an automatic death penalty for people in the country illegally who commit capital offenses.

abortion.summary: Grow's campaign site identifies him as a pro-life Republican. He does not describe any circumstances in which he would loosen Florida's six-week law.

guns.summary: Grow says he voted for open carry and describes himself as a pro-Second Amendment Republican who voted to protect Second Amendment rights.

healthcare.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

social_security.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

education_choice.summary: Grow describes himself as a strong supporter of school choice and of empowering parents, and cites votes expanding student transportation access and allowing home-schooled children to play school sports.

environment.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

growth.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

marijuana.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

elections.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

crime.summary: Grow's campaign site highlights what it calls his unwavering support of law enforcement, and he cites votes for increased funding for detention and enforcement.

lgbtq.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

energy.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

trump.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

veterans.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

record.item: Voted for CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; a vote to refer the amendment is coded as leaning.
Says he voted for a state budget that funds free health care for more than 200,000 Florida children each year.
Says he voted to revise school start times and to expand student transportation access and sports participation for home-schooled children.
